text:
alex_fin: Heads up — vendor Metrika sent invoice INV-26078 for €45,000 and used a German VAT ID, but billing address is UK. VAT line shows 20% charged. Can finance confirm whether we should gross-up or treat as reverse charge?

maria_sales: Do we have PO 4432? They sold via EMEA sales. I think they should be reverse-charged (B2B), but need VAT ID validation.

oliver_ops: I've checked their GB VAT number against VIES, it returns INVALID. They gave DE number which validates. Invoice has 'ship to' UK office but bill-to is DE entity.

alex_fin: If bill-to is DE legal entity, then German VAT applies. But our tax ops needs to confirm entity mapping. @emily_legal can you weigh in?

emily_legal: Quick take: if supplier is a DE-registered company issuing to our UK branch, then VAT treatment depends on whether supply is to our UK legal entity or to Redwood EU entity. We need W-8/W-9? not for EU. Please confirm customer VAT IDs. If reverse charge, we won't pay VAT but need supplier to reissue w/o VAT.

tax_bot: VIES check: DE123456789 — Valid; GB987654321 — Not found. Flagging invoice INV-26078 as 'VAT mismatch' in Zendesk ticket #Z-512.

anna_vendor: Hi Alex — Metrika here. We billed our German legal entity by mistake. Can reissue invoice to Redwood Ltd (UK) with no VAT and a note for reverse charge. Will send corrected PDF today.

maria_sales: :thumbsup: please make sure new invoice references PO 4432 and include GB VAT ID once we have it.

alex_fin: Thanks — I'll hold payment until corrected invoice. If reissue not possible we may request gross-up quote. Tagging @oliver_ops to update vendor record.

oliver_ops: Updating vendor record now. Setting 'needs corrected invoice' flag. Putting payment on hold.
